headline: Spatial atlases and quantitative metrics resolve tissue architecture and rare cells
label: Spatial Cell Atlases Across Tissues
summary: Spatial omics now pairs reference-scale atlases with metrics that correct size bias and score rare cells, extending tissue-level inference.
synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving cell identity and spatial organization within intact tissue. A 128-patient prostate cancer single-cell and spatial atlas maps gene modules underlying lineage plasticity and metastasis, and a benchmark of five single-cell tumor immune atlases shows supervised annotation outperforming clustering for immunotherapy-related cell states. The methodological layer is quantitative: MINGL converts spatial-omics neighborhood annotations into continuous measures of borders and gradients, ClumPyCells corrects aggregation metrics for cell size bias, and RareQ scores k-nearest-neighbor cliquishness to detect rare cells. Mechanistic models of fibrosis and ER+ breast cancer stroma add simulated fibroblast and CAF dynamics. What is new is the shift from descriptive atlases toward metrics that quantify architecture directly in tissue context.
